title: Microbootstrap Terraform composer for EKS API plane provisioning and safe upgrades
creator: Diego Morales
description:
Build a composable Terraform module ("microbootstrap") responsible for provisioning the EKS API/control plane components used in Redwood Private VPC deployments.

Scope: idempotent creation of control-plane IAM roles and policies, KMS/WrappingKey bindings for cross-account envelope encryption, EKS control-plane settings (endpoint access, logging config), preflight checks, automated canary cluster rollout hooks, and a lightweight health probe framework that integrates with the existing observability playbook. Module must be opinionated enough to enforce security posture yet extensible for enterprise overrides (e.g., custom CNI, private endpoints).
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module exposes a simple root input set (vpc_id, management_account_id, kms_key_arn, cluster_name, control_plane_tags) and contains sane defaults for production: private endpoint, controlPlaneLogging = true, strict IAM least-privilege roles.
Module applies idempotently across multiple runs and renders no diffs when applied twice with identical inputs (documented test steps).

Upgrade hooks: module supports a declarative 'upgrade_phase' toggle that wires preflight probes, a canary control-plane rollout (single-az small cluster), and automatic traffic migration plan for Dedicated mode.

Health probe framework publishes a Prometheus-compatible metric (redwood.priv_controlplane.health) and writes human-readable incidents to the infra incident dashboard for any failing preflight or post-upgrade checks.
Integration tests (Terraform validate + terratest-like integration) run in CI and a documented manual canary runbook exists in Confluence with rollback steps and PR links.
updates: 2026-01-21 — Ticket created. Spike completed last week: validated that a lightweight composer approach (module calling smaller submodules) reduces repeated code across regions. Decided to prefer composition over monolith to ease QA of upgrade hooks.

2026-01-28 — Design review with Security (Leah Kim) and Networking (Samir Reddy). Security requested explicit KMS grant rotation and support for external HSM ARNs. Added to scope; tracking as design requirement.

2026-02-04 — Prototype landed: root module and 2 submodules (iam-roles, api-plane-config). Integration smoke apply in dev-account succeeded. Observability stubs created that emit metrics to the dev Grafana dashboard.

2026-02-16 — PR #6221 opened for initial module plus example app. Review feedback from infra team: tighten IAM statements (deny wildcards), add preflight for controlPlaneLogging, and fail-fast on deprecated AMIs used by node pools. Addressing comments.

2026-02-25 — Implemented canary-aware upgrade hook: when 'upgrade_phase' set to 'canary', module spawns a small canary control-plane (separate cluster resource with a suffix) and wires route53 traffic weights for Dedicated staging. Added a migration plan generator script (Python) to compute traffic shift steps.

2026-03-01 — Added terratest-compatible integration tests and a basic chaos test (simulated control-plane API throttling) to ensure graceful fallbacks. Test flake on CI due to account quota; chasing quota increase with cloud-ops.

2026-03-05 — Security review scheduled for 2026-03-09. Blocker: cross-account KMS grant TTL behaviour requires infra policy clarification (pinged cloud security). Next actions: finalize KMS grant rotation design, finish PR comment remediation, and run a manual canary in staging.
open_questions: Should the module own control-plane logging configuration by default or expose it as a required input so security can enforce central logging? (Security prefers required input.)
Do we rely on Route53 weighted records for Dedicated canary migration or integrate with the Smart Routing service? Smart Routing might provide better observability but increases coupling.
What is the expected rollback SLA for a failed control-plane upgrade? We need to formalize rollback time and automation level in the runbook.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: KMS cross-account grant expiry causing control-plane failure. Mitigation: implement automated grant rotation and add a preflight check that validates grant presence before upgrades.
Risk: Terraform race conditions during simultaneous cluster and IAM changes. Mitigation: split resources into separate apply stages and provide explicit apply targets in the supported runbook.

Risk: Canary canister remains in flight if route53 weights are misapplied. Mitigation: add a safety TTL and automatic revert script if health metrics dip below threshold within the observation window.
next_steps: Finish addressing PR feedback and update module to use explicit IAM conditions (no wildcards).
Complete Security review and add HSM/KMS guidance to the Confluence design doc.
Coordinate quota increase with cloud-ops to stabilize CI integration tests.
Run manual canary in staging week of 2026-03-15, collect health metrics and iterate on rollback automation if needed.
